- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Require verified release-fixture provenance before silencing alerts; do not use an author-controlled title as the suppression criterion." (Issue #6341, Recommendation.)
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml, parent-fixture silence block at lines 142-156 (the path that resolves `Tracking issue: #<N>` from the issue body and reads that tracking issue's title).
  Evidence of absence: The PR hardens the issue-title path at lines 129-135 with a `.user.type == "User" and .author_association IN("OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR")` predicate, but the parent-fixture block at lines 142-156 still sets `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL=SILENT` based solely on the tracked issue's title matching `^\[Orchestrator\] E2E `:
  ```
  154:             if printf '%s' "${TRACKING_TITLE}" | grep -qiE '^\[Orchestrator\] E2E '; then
  155:               echo "🔬 Smoke orchestrator parent (#${TRACKING_NUM}) — suppressing per-phase Telegram alerts"
  156:               echo "ALERT_MSG_LEVEL=SILENT" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
  ```
  No author-association predicate is applied to the tracking-issue payload (`TRACKING_PAYLOAD`); no `AI_PHASE_GATE_V1 ... gate=smoke_alert_silence ...` branch exists for this path; the new contract test `test_issue_title_silencing_requires_trusted_author` only inspects the block up to the `Resolve integration ref` step and never enters this region. A standalone issue whose body contains `Tracking issue: #<N>` where issue #N is a tracking issue with title `[Orchestrator] E2E Smoke Test` (author-controlled: any actor can create such a tracking issue) reaches the gate and still has alerts suppressed for worker failure, escalation, or any other clarify-respond path that consults `$ALERT_MSG_LEVEL` — exactly the bypass the issue describes.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  WHY: An attacker can create a standalone issue with `Tracking issue: #<E2E-tracker>` in the body. The PR fixes the direct `[E2E ...]` path but leaves this second silencing path title-only, which is the exact attack vector issue #6341 identifies.

  WHY: This is not a runtime correctness bug in the new code itself; committing these unrelated changes to the same PR bundles two distinct fixes and makes them harder to bisect, revert, or review in isolation.
